epic.name: Approve or reject a request
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify a second decision is genuinely refused: because the service answers the same way whether a decision was recorded or refused, the app decides 'already decided' by re-reading the request just before it submits. If the service actually accepts a second decision, one approver could overwrite another's decision without either of them seeing anything wrong.

Verify the right person is named as the decider: the app sends the signed-in person's first and last name as who made the decision. If the service expects a username or an email address instead, 'Last changed by' could name nobody recognisable, or be blank, on every decision recorded from now on.

Verify a decision shows immediately: after you approve or reject, the app re-reads the request list to show the new status. If the service records the decision but takes a moment to report it, the request may still read Imported straight after you decided it, and look as though nothing happened.

Verify the payments service accepts a decision on the strength of your sign-in alone: the app passes your existing session along when it records a decision. If that service expects something else for a server-to-server call, every decision will come back refused even though you are properly signed in — worth watching on the very first live approval.
